**Blocking: 5 majors open.** Round 1 · 5 majors open · 5 nits · 5 pre-existing

| Severity | Where | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 Major | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:515` | --benchmark-skip grep assertion can never fail | new |
| 🟡 Nit | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:373` | 548-day oracle corpus is one shape, 548 times | new |
| 🟡 Nit | `src/local_fitness/agent/tools.py:169` | Docstring says bool guard is now load-bearing; it isn't | new |
| 🟡 Nit | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:16` | Third axis is skipped by the only run the docstring names | new |
| 🟡 Nit | `CLAUDE.md:161` | CLAUDE.md perf bullet still says two axes, not three | new |
| 🟡 Nit | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:428` | json.dumps oracle can't see tuple vs list | new |
| 🟣 Pre-existing | `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1205` | grade_workout re-walks the day list just walked | new |
| 🟣 Pre-existing | `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1259` | grade_workout still re-walks the same day's activities | new |
| 🟣 Pre-existing | `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1212` | _ran redoes the _is_on_foot check the loop just did | new |
| 🔴 Major | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:297` | round_floats count bound goes red on 2026-09-22 | new |
| 🟣 Pre-existing | `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1259` | grade_workout re-walks the list _workout_actuals walked | new |
| 🟣 Pre-existing | `src/local_fitness/plans.py:339` | classify_workout re-derives what _workout_actuals returns | new |
| 🔴 Major | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:284` | _ran<=90 passes vacuously when no plan is active | new |
| 🔴 Major | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:297` | _round_floats<=100 passes vacuously on an empty payload | new |
| 🔴 Major | `tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py:373` | 548-day oracle corpus is 548 copies of one case | new |

**Could not anchor** — GitHub refused a thread on these lines; they still count:

- 🟡 `CLAUDE.md:161` — The PR adds a third assertion axis to the perf suite and edits the same CLAUDE.md bullet, but leaves that bullet's description of what the suite asserts at "latency AND `db.connect()`-open-count". (f-6c527dc9)
- 🟣 `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1259` — The fold removes only 36 of the handler's 87 `_ran` evaluations; the other 51 come from `grade_workout` re-walking the very same day list three more times in the same loop iteration, which is the identical defect class the diff was sent to fix. (f-0e170358)
- 🟣 `src/local_fitness/plans.py:1259` — The fold removes one of four passes over each day's activity list, but `grade_workout` on the very next line and `weekly_mileage` further down re-walk the same list through `_running_distance`/`_foot_distance`/`_running_duration`, so 51 of the 87 remaining `_ran` evaluations are still second-pass work the diff's docstring says no longer exists. (f-87bad23f)
- 🟣 `src/local_fitness/plans.py:339` — `classify_workout` re-derives the running/foot distance for a day that `_workout_actuals` has already computed and returned in the same `build_plan_detail` iteration — the folded five-tuple is the existing helper the grading branch should be reading. (f-708c84ed)

Plus 20 more nits not posted inline (cap 5).

<details><summary>Not examined</summary>

- The six pytest-benchmark latency targets themselves and the committed `.benchmarks/Linux-CPython-3.12-64bit/0001_*.json` baseline — untouched by the diff, and I did not re-run a timed comparison or verify the projected +7%/+12% outcome (Proof 8, explicitly labelled 'not a test').
- The factual accuracy of the narrative claims added to CLAUDE.md and CHANGELOG.md about CI history — run `33652312669`, the EPYC 7763 clock pair, the -0.34%/+13.86% readings, the bisect to `b28c74e`, and the CPython 3.12.13-vs-3.12.14 note. These name external CI artifacts I cannot read offline.
- `docs/plans/2026-07-09-mcp-speed-and-ui-retirement-design.md`, which also documents the 15% gate and which the plan deliberately left untouched — I did not audit it for staleness against the new third axis.
- The other three work items on issue #232 (`notes-update-handle-collision`, `notes-archive-failure-preserves-live`, `notes-undated-eviction-order`) and `src/local_fitness/notes.py` — outside this lane's diff.
- `tests/test_plans.py` beyond the four retargeted `_normalize_activity_types` tests and the comment at :566 — I read the renamed tests and confirmed they exercise the same inputs through `_workout_actuals()[4]`, but did not audit the rest of the file.
- Whether real (non-fixture) `get_training_plan_progress` payloads ever contain `dict`/`list` subclasses or tuples that would take the slow `isinstance` fallback — I verified the fallback is semantically identical, not how often it is hit in production.
- The report-card path (`rc_db`, `build_report_card_fixture_db`) and the other four benchmarked handlers — `_round_floats` is shared by all 55+ tools via `_text`/`_err`, and I verified equivalence generically rather than per-tool payload.
- Sections of CLAUDE.md outside those governing perf benchmarks, testing/workflow expectations, and run-vs-walk classification (roughly lines 286-1664 were skimmed by heading only).
- The pytest-benchmark latency baseline itself (.benchmarks/Linux-CPython-3.12-64bit/0001_*.json) — not in the diff, and its committed values cannot be re-measured on this machine (Darwin-CPython-3.12-64bit).
- The CHANGELOG's measured claims of '-6.0% (p05, interleaved in-process A/B)' and '49.6% of this function's own runtime' — I verified the two call counts (87 and 83 at this head, matching) but did not re-run a timing A/B.
- The CPython 3.12.13 vs 3.12.14 interpreter question recorded as open in the new CLAUDE.md text — not resolvable without a capture-perf-baseline.yml dispatch.
- The four other benchmark targets (assemble_brief_context, get_training_plan_status, _build_plan_section, daily_snapshot) and the report-card path — untouched by the diff except through the shared `_round_floats`, which the fuzz covered generically.
- tests/test_plans.py beyond the four renamed activity-type tests and their two neighbours (lines 553-610).
- The three notes.py items (1-3) from issue #232 — this work item is the perf half only; they belong to other lanes.
- The PR page, its CI run history, and any review comments — the brief says the diff and the checkout are the source.
- Whether the `docs/plans/2026-06-23-*` design docs that describe `_workout_actuals`'s signature need updating for the fold; I confirmed they do not name `_normalize_activity_types`, but did not read them in full.
- The CHANGELOG.md and CLAUDE.md prose hunks were read for claims to check against the code, but not reviewed as documentation (wording, placement, house style) — that is the conventions angle, not mine.
- The pytest-benchmark latency baseline artifact itself (.benchmarks/ / the committed 0001_*.json) — I did not open it or re-run `--benchmark-only`, so I cannot say whether the -6.0% claim reproduces on this machine.
- The 84 test failures in tests/test_visuals.py and tests/test_tools.py on this machine are all WeasyPrint `OSError: cannot load library 'libgobject-2.0-0'` and were treated as environmental, not diffed against the base commit to prove they pre-exist.
- `plans.grade_workout`/`classify_workout` grading semantics beyond the `_ran` call-count question — I checked which helpers they call over the same list, not whether their verdicts are correct.
- Non-`get_training_plan_progress` consumers of `_round_floats` beyond `_text`, `_err` and `mcp_server._render_status` — I confirmed by grep those are the only three call sites but did not enumerate what each of the 55+ tools puts through it, so an exotic payload type (a `Decimal`, a `datetime`, a dataclass) reaching the new fast path is reasoned about from the code, not observed.
- The `full=true` branch of the handler and `get_training_plan_status`/`_build_plan_section`, which share `build_plan_detail`'s day lists — I did not instrument their call counts.
- scripts/perf_fixture.py's construction (how many activity days, how long the seeded plan is) beyond confirming `len(by_date) > 500` holds — the fixture-shape sensitivity in the `<= 90` candidate is reasoned from the call-site arithmetic, not from reading the generator.
- Whether PR #236's CI has actually run these tests, and on which date — I read the checkout and the diff file only, never the pull request page.
- The three notes lanes of issue #232 (items 1-3) — this PR is the perf lane only and touches no notes code; I read their plan sections purely to confirm nothing in this diff belongs to them.
- Whether the projected post-fix CI numbers (+7.1% on a baseline-matching runner, +11.7% on the slowest observed) actually land — the plan itself labels that 'observable, not a test', and I did not dispatch or read any CI run.
- The absolute latency claims in the CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.md (-6.0% p05, 49.6% of the function's own runtime, the 2026-09-02 run tables, the b28c74e bisect). I re-derived the deterministic counts (87 _ran, 83 _round_floats, 10,122 payload bytes — all exact) but ran no timing A/B and did not verify the two GitHub run ids or their machine_info.
- The conventions angle against CLAUDE.md — not one of my two assigned angles (intent, simplification); another finder is carrying it.
- Correctness of the CLAUDE.md prose addition as English/policy (whether the 'apply the tell per benchmark' rule is the right rule) — I only checked that it is present and matches what the plan asked for.
- 84 test failures in the full local suite (53 in tests/test_visuals.py, 31 in tests/test_tools.py) — all WeasyPrint 'cannot load library libgobject-2.0-0' dlopen errors, a known macOS DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH environment gap unrelated to this diff. I did not re-run them with the env var set or confirm them on the base commit.
- pyproject.toml version bump / release wiring — the plan explicitly defers the bump to whichever of the four items lands last, so its absence here is by design and I did not audit the release path.
- Whether `docs/plans/2026-07-09-mcp-speed-and-ui-retirement-design.md` should have been updated now that the suite asserts three axes rather than two; I confirmed the design doc does not enumerate the axes and that tests/test_docs_drift.py only covers docs/mcp/, so there is no automated drift, but I did not read the design doc in full.

</details>

threads.body:
<!-- issueflow:finding f-9674e7de -->
🔴 **Major** · `f-9674e7de` · line-by-line · CONFIRMED

The `--benchmark-skip` half of `test_the_latency_gate_is_still_armed` cannot fail: `pyproject.toml` line 55 is a comment that begins `# --benchmark-skip:`, so the substring survives deletion of the flag from `addopts`.

**Failure scenario.** Verified: `sed '59s/ --benchmark-skip//' pyproject.toml | grep -c -- '--benchmark-skip'` returns 1 — the comment at pyproject.toml:55 ("# --benchmark-skip: the perf-benchmark suite (tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py) / only runs when explicitly requested via --benchmark-only...") keeps the string alive. Someone removes `--benchmark-skip` from `addopts` (line 59); every ordinary `uv run pytest` then runs the six timed latency benchmarks, and the test whose docstring says it guards "the `--benchmark-skip` default that keeps these benchmarks off an ordinary `pytest` run" stays green. Directly against CLAUDE.md:113-125: "The bar is 'would this test FAIL if the code under test were broken?' — if not, it isn't a test." (The sibling assertion on line 513 is sound: `--benchmark-compare-fail=min:15%` appears exactly once in ci.yml, in the run command at :72, with no comment mentioning it.)

> assert "--benchmark-skip" in (root / "pyproject.toml").read_text()

```suggestion
    import tomllib
    addopts = tomllib.loads((root / "pyproject.toml").read_text())["tool"]["pytest"]["ini_options"]["addopts"]
    assert "--benchmark-skip" in addopts
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-73a7ebc6 -->
🟡 **Nit** · `f-73a7ebc6` · line-by-line · CONFIRMED

The equivalence oracle's anti-vacuity floor (`assert len(by_date) > 500`) presents a 548-day corpus that is measurably one input shape repeated 548 times, and neither it nor the six edge cases contains a multi-activity day — the exact case the fold changed.

**Failure scenario.** Measured against the real fixture (scripts/perf_fixture.py:196-206 seeds one row per date, always `activity_type='running'`, always with no `avg_pace_sec_per_km`): 548 days, max 1 activity/day, exactly 1 distinct classification shape `(('running', paceless, dist>0),)`, and every single day returns `['running']`. The `walking` branch, the `other` branch and every multi-activity list are never differentially compared. The fold's actual control-flow change is that `classes.add('other')` now runs inside the loop that accumulates `foot`/`dur` and hits `continue` before the distance work — so a day holding one on-foot activity and one ride is the case that would catch an ordering or accumulation mistake, and no case in `_WORKOUT_ACTUALS_EDGE_CASES` (all six are single-activity) or in the 548-day loop is one. Combined with `test_workout_actuals_evaluates_ran_once_per_on_foot_activity` (:269), which passes a mixed 3-activity day but asserts only the `_ran` count and never the returned classes, the mixed-day fold is differentially untested here; only `tests/test_plans.py:test_workout_actuals_returns_foot_run_and_walk_in_one_pass` covers it, and it is not an oracle against the pre-fold implementation. Same CLAUDE.md rule as above ("never coverage theater", :113-125) plus its "Cover the edge cases" clause.

> assert len(by_date) > 500

```suggestion
Add a mixed day to `_WORKOUT_ACTUALS_EDGE_CASES`, e.g. `[_PACED_RUN, _PACED_WALK, _RIDE, {"activity_type": None, "distance_meters": 100.0}]`, and assert a floor on `len(_WORKOUT_ACTUALS_EDGE_CASES)` the way `_ROUND_FLOATS_CASES` does at :506.
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-0dd0d0da -->
🟡 **Nit** · `f-0dd0d0da` · line-by-line · CONFIRMED

The new docstring parenthetical claims the `bool` guard "becomes load-bearing" under the fast path and forbids any test showing otherwise; measured, the guard is still completely inert after this change.

**Failure scenario.** Deleted `if isinstance(obj, bool): return obj` (tools.py:187-188) from the post-change implementation and differentially fuzzed it against the pre-inline reference over 40,000 randomly generated nested payloads (dicts/lists/dict-subclass/list-subclass containers; leaves covering float, float/int subclasses, bool, int, str, None, NaN, +/-inf, -0.0, tuple, bytes, Decimal, date, frozenset, OrderedDict; high-precision and non-string keys), comparing structurally with type preservation, not via json.dumps: 0 divergences — identical to the 0 divergences the unmodified new implementation produces. The reason is that the guard was never reachable in a way that mattered and still isn't: both container fast paths copy a `bool` child inline via `t is bool` (lines 199, 211) and never recurse for it, and the fallback `isinstance` ladder (lines 220-225) still has no `int` branch, so a bool arriving at the top falls all the way through to `return obj` unchanged. There is no `int` fast path that rounds — line 199/211 only copy. Cost: the comment states a false invariant about the code three lines below it, and instructs the next author ("no test may claim removing it is observable") on the strength of that false reason, so the guard's real status — dead-but-harmless defensive code — is now recorded backwards in the one place a reader checks.

> below makes it load-bearing, so it stays and no test may claim removing it

<!-- issueflow:finding f-63b3df6d -->
🟡 **Nit** · `f-63b3df6d` · line-by-line · CONFIRMED

The new third axis never runs in the invocation this file's own docstring says is the only one that runs it — `--benchmark-only` skips every non-benchmark test, so all six new tests are skipped in CI's perf-gate step.

**Failure scenario.** Ran it: `pytest tests/test_perf_benchmarks.py --benchmark-only` reports `6 passed, 16 skipped` with `SKIPPED [16] Skipping non-benchmark (--benchmark-only active).` — pytest-benchmark's `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (plugin.py:336-347) marks every item without the `benchmark` fixture skipped under `--benchmark-only`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:70` is exactly that invocation, so the entire work-COUNT axis and both equivalence oracles are skipped in the "Perf-benchmark regression gate" step and only execute in the "Run tests with coverage gate" step. Lines 4-7 of this same docstring — unchanged by the diff — say "a plain `uv run pytest` never runs the ... benchmarks here — only an explicit `--benchmark-only` invocation does", and the diff appends "Three axes are asserted" under it. A maintainer debugging a red perf gate reads that header, expects the work counts to be part of what the gate reported, and will not find them; a maintainer adding a fourth work-count assertion will reasonably put it behind the `benchmark` fixture and silently disable it in the coverage job instead. The axis does run in CI (in the other step), so this is a documentation/placement defect, not dead code.

> * work COUNT (added 2026-09-03, #232) — the same counter pointed at the

```suggestion
Add one sentence to the axis list saying the work-COUNT axis runs in the ordinary `pytest` job and is skipped under `--benchmark-only`, the inverse of the latency axis.
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-7ede0eb0 -->
🟡 **Nit** · `f-7ede0eb0` · line-by-line · CONFIRMED

`_dumped`'s `json.dumps` comparison is type-blind, so the oracle cannot assert the tuple-to-list conversion the cases at :412 and :413 exist to cover, nor any container/scalar subclass identity.

**Failure scenario.** `json.dumps((1.23, 2.35)) == json.dumps([1.23, 2.35]) == '[1.23, 2.35]'`, and `default=str` further collapses anything unserializable to its `str()`. The approved plan's Proof 5 names "a `tuple` (must become a `list`)" as a required case and `_ROUND_FLOATS_CASES` duly carries `(1.23456789, 2.3456789)` and `[(1.23456789,), (2.3456789,)]` — but the comparison function cannot distinguish pass from fail on that property. A later fast-path extension such as `if type(obj) is tuple: return obj` (a tempting next optimization, since tuples currently take the slow ladder) changes `_round_floats`'s return type contract and leaves both oracle tests green. The same blindness covers `_FloatSubclass`/`_IntSubclass`/`_DictSubclass`: `_mishandles_a_dict_subclass` only diverges because its *values* stay unrounded, not because its type differs, so the two-sidedness proof at :463 does not demonstrate type coverage either. (For the record, a type-preserving 40k-case differential fuzz confirms the shipped implementation IS equivalent today — the gap is that the committed oracle would not notice if it stopped being.)

> return json.dumps(obj, default=str)

```suggestion
Compare with a type-preserving normalizer, or add one direct assertion: `assert isinstance(tools._round_floats((1.0, 2.0)), list)`.
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-8e190b4d -->
🟣 **Pre-existing** · `f-8e190b4d` · efficiency · CONFIRMED

The fold removes one redundant pass over the day's activity list but leaves another in the same caller loop: `classify_workout` recomputes `_running_distance`/`_foot_distance`, values `_workout_actuals` returned two lines earlier.

**Failure scenario.** In `build_plan_detail` (plans.py:1254-1257) each iteration calls `_workout_actuals(day, cfg)` — which returns `foot` and `run_m` — and then immediately `grade_workout(w, day, frontier, cfg)`, whose `classify_workout` recomputes `_foot_distance(day_activities)` (plans.py:337) or `_running_distance(day_activities, cfg)` (plans.py:339) or `_running_duration(day_activities, cfg)` (plans.py:351) over the same list, evaluating `_ran` once more per activity. Because `_ran` checks on-foot first (plans.py:165-166, "ON-FOOT IS CHECKED FIRST"), `_running_distance(day, cfg)` is exactly the `run_m` already in hand and `_foot_distance(day)` is exactly `foot` — the recomputation is byte-identical work. Measured on the perf fixture at this head: the handler still makes 87 `_ran` calls (and 83 `_round_floats` calls) for one `get_training_plan_progress` request; the fold's own accounting (one `_ran` per on-foot activity) implies roughly a third of that. Cheaper alternative: have `_workout_actuals` also accumulate running duration and pass its five/six-tuple into `grade_workout`/`classify_workout` instead of letting them re-derive it. This predates the diff, but the diff's new docstring sentence on this very line — "Anything else this day needs is computed in the loop below, not in a pass of its own" — is contradicted by the next statement in its only caller, so the invariant it re-asserts is still not true at the handler level.

> threshold for five weeks. Anything else this day needs is computed in the

<!-- issueflow:finding f-d44090f3 -->
🟣 **Pre-existing** · `f-d44090f3` · altitude · CONFIRMED

Inside the loop this diff rewrote, `_ran(a, cfg)` re-runs the `_is_on_foot` substring scan that the line above already computed, so the loop does more label-matching work than the `_ran` count it optimises.

**Failure scenario.** plans.py:1222 computes `_is_on_foot(at)` and `continue`s when it is False; line 1231 then calls `_ran(a, cfg)`, whose first statement (plans.py:167-169) is `if not _is_on_foot(at): return False` — the identical call on the identical value. Measured at the head commit on the perf fixture, one `get_training_plan_progress` request over 36 activities: `_is_on_foot` 139 calls and `_is_running` 226 calls, against 87 `_ran` calls. `_is_running`/`_is_walking` each lowercase the label and run an `any(...)` substring scan over a frozenset, so this is strictly more work per activity than the `_ran` dispatch the diff counts — and the new assertion counts `_ran` only, so the duplication is invisible to the gate the change adds. The deeper fix in the lines the diff already touches: split `_ran` into an on-foot-known variant (or hoist `at.lower()` once per activity) so the loop's known-on-foot branch does not pay for the check a second time. Cleanup, not a crash.

> if not _is_on_foot(at):

<!-- issueflow:finding f-eea114d4 -->
🔴 **Major** · `f-eea114d4` · cross-file · CONFIRMED

The new `_round_floats` work-count bound `counts["n"] <= 100` is not deterministic across dates — the count it measures grows with `date.today()` because `get_training_plan_progress`'s default window is `max(frontier, today) + 7d`, so the assertion goes permanently red on 2026-09-22, 17 days after this head commit, with no code change.

**Failure scenario.** Executed in this checkout at 776ccbd, with `tools.date.today()` faked and everything else untouched: the `_round_floats` call count for `get_training_plan_progress.handler({})` against the module-scoped `perf_db` (built with `today=date(2026,7,9)`) is 25 on 2026-07-09, 79 on 2026-09-01, 83 on 2026-09-05 (real today), 101 on 2026-09-22 — the first date the `<= 100` assertion fails — 109 on 2026-09-30, and it plateaus at 115 from 2026-10-06 onward. The mechanism is cross-file: the handler (src/local_fitness/agent/tools.py:3850-3854) sets `anchor_fwd = max(frontier or today, today)` and `window_end = anchor_fwd + 7d`, so every extra day of wall clock past the fixture's frontier sweeps another prescribed workout dict into `workouts_full`, and each extra dict is one more `_round_floats` recursion. `_ran` is immune (87 at every date probed) only because `build_plan_detail` grades the full plan; the serialized payload is the windowed one. This is the failure class issue #232 item 4 names — a today-relative fixture under a hard-coded expectation — and the test's own header comment at line 285 claims the opposite of it: "they are deterministic, they do not care which CPU CI drew".

> assert counts["n"] <= 100

```suggestion
Freeze the clock for the two work-count tests the way the repo already does elsewhere (`tests/test_tools.py:3797` `_freeze_ledger_clock`, `tests/test_mcp_server.py:790`): `monkeypatch.setattr(tools, "date", _FakeDate)` pinned to `_TODAY` before calling the handler, then assert the exact count (83 at `_TODAY + 58d`, 25 at `_TODAY`) rather than a `<=` bound.
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-0583160f -->
🔴 **Major** · `f-0583160f` · intent · CONFIRMED

The handler-level `_ran` count assertion is an upper bound with no floor and no payload check, so it passes over zero work whenever the handler returns early.

**Failure scenario.** `get_training_plan_progress.handler` returns `_text({"active": False})` at tools.py:3765 whenever `plans.get_active_plan` is None. Measured in the worktree: with the perf fixture's plan row flipped to status='completed', `plans._ran` is called 0 times and the assertion `counts["n"] <= 90` passes green. Proof 2 in the plan is the one that says the fold actually reached the handler ('proof 1 alone can be satisfied by a folded helper nobody calls'), and it stops saying that the moment `_seed_plan` drifts, `get_active_plan`'s status filter changes, or the fixture's plan ages out. The sibling oracle test at :455 already carries the guard this one lacks (`assert payload.get("workouts")`), and this same diff writes an explicit anti-vacuity floor at :373 with the comment 'A query that quietly matched nothing must fail here, not pass over an empty loop' — so the change applies the rule to one of its three new count assertions and not to the other two.

> assert counts["n"] <= 90

```suggestion
    assert 60 <= counts["n"] <= 90
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-7098c483 -->
🔴 **Major** · `f-7098c483` · intent · CONFIRMED

The `_round_floats` count assertion has the same vacuity hole — an early-return handler produces exactly one call, which is comfortably under the bound.

**Failure scenario.** Measured in the worktree with no active plan: `_text({"active": False})` drives `tools._round_floats` exactly 1 time, and `assert counts["n"] <= 100` passes. Its own docstring calls it 'the assertion that binds the `_round_floats` change to a real reduction in work', which is exactly the claim that evaporates: a 1-call run and an 83-call run are indistinguishable to it. Anything that shrinks the fixture payload — a plan that stops seeding, `build_plan_detail` projecting fewer fields, a future compaction pass — silently converts this from a work-count proof into a tautology, and unlike a latency reading nothing else in CI would notice.

> assert counts["n"] <= 100

```suggestion
    assert 60 <= counts["n"] <= 100
```

<!-- issueflow:finding f-7115b02e -->
🔴 **Major** · `f-7115b02e` · intent · CONFIRMED

The `_workout_actuals` equivalence oracle's '548 activity-days' corpus is 548 copies of a single shape, so its anti-vacuity floor counts days rather than distinct behaviour.

**Failure scenario.** Measured against `build_perf_fixture_db` in the worktree: 548 dates, every one holding exactly 1 activity, all 548 typed `running`, and `avg_pace_sec_per_km` NULL on all 548 (scripts/perf_fixture.py:50-60 makes the paceless-ness deliberate). Every single day therefore returns `('running',)` via `_ran`'s label fallback — one branch, 548 times.
